messages:
devon: heads up — seeing the quickquota panel show another org's committed quota to a few users in staging and once in prod. @frances can you take a look? :rotating_light:
frances: saw a blip in telemetry an hour ago, thought it was noise. can you repro and paste traces? :eyes:
devon: repro steps: open console -> QuickQuota widget -> switch org quickly. observed widget display `orgId: 4321` while my session is org 1234. repro on staging consistently.
sam: can you paste the request/response headers?
devon: here's the trace snippet:
```
GET /prefetch/widget/quickquota?widget=42 HTTP/1.1
Host: console.internal
X-Org-ID: 1234
X-User: devon
Cache-Key: pref:quickquota::widget=42
Response-Body: {"orgId":4321, "quota": 1200}
```
frances: nailed it — cache key missing tenant component. the `prefetch-v2` key encoder changed to dedupe by widget+params but dropped org. that explains cross-tenant payload reuse.
kai: was prefetch-v2 on a canary rollout?
frances: yes, traffic split 10% canary earlier today behind feature flag. we tightened latency but missed tenant in key template.
bella: immediate mitigation: rollback canary and purge affected keys. anyone object to pausing rollout?
ash: hotfix idea: add a short guard where if cached payload.org != request.X-Org-ID, we return 403 or bypass cache and emit metric. safer than immediate purge in case of large scale.
frances: agree with both — rollback + hotfix guard. plan: 1) sam rollback canary to 0% (now) 2) devon run targeted cache purge for keys since 11:00UTC 3) I’ll PR encoder change to include org and add unit tests 4) kai add telemetry alert `console.prefetch.cache.org_mismatch`
sam: rolling prefetch-v2 back to 0% now.
deploy-bot: deploy request received: rollback prefetch-v2 canary -> executing
deploy-bot: rollback complete — canary=0% ✅
frances: opening PR for encoder fix — will include new key pattern: `pref:{org}:{widget}:{params_hash}` and assertion in encoder. adding e2e to verify header propagation. tagging @security and @customer-ops for review.
kai: will add a temporary alert: emit when any cache hit returns payload.org != request.org. set paging threshold = 1. also add a daily report of unique cache keys missing org.
devon: I found ~18 unique keys in staging matching the pattern and one in prod for acme-inc (reported incident at 11:23UTC). emailed CSM already.
frances: thanks. after encoder PR and tests we re-enable canary only after cache purge + 24h observation window.
bella: small follow-ups: add a lint rule for cache-key templates to require `{org}` token and update runbook for prefetch rollouts.
ash: also recommend a safety harness in the runtime: if payload.age > 1h and request.org not in allowlist, bypass cache and emit debug log.
frances: agreed. I'll capture action items in the incident and post to #incidents.
devon: leaving note to scrub any cached payloads that include `orgId` fields before re-enabling.
sam: ack — will include in rollback ticket and follow up with postmortem in eng-platform.
